note: Hebrew 'asherim are wooden cult objects (poles or stylised trees) associated with the goddess Asherah, not groves of trees.
Hebrew matstsevot are upright standing stones (cultic pillars), not images or statues; the carved images (pesilim) are listed separately.

mine: a people for His treasured possession
note: Hebrew 'am segullah means a people that is his personal treasure; "special" has lost the sense of private property.
Hebrew dagan is cereal grain generally (wheat, barley); "corn" now suggests maize to many readers.
Hebrew massot, the testing ordeals of the plagues (cf. 4:34); "temptations" now implies enticement to sin.

kjv: shall destroy them (the nations) with a mighty destruction
mine: throw them (the nations) into great confusion
note: Hebrew hamam ... mehumah gedolah means to throw into great panic or confusion (the divine terror of holy war); the destruction follows ("until they are destroyed").

kjv: lest thou be a cursed thing like it (the abomination)
mine: or you will become devoted to destruction like it (the abomination)
note: Hebrew cherem is something set apart for God by destruction (the "ban", cf. v.2 hacharem tacharim); "cursed thing" loses the link with the herem command.
